figures.finding: A resident's work income (pay and non-commercial income) is taxed after allowances at 0% to XAF 800,000 a year, 10.5% to 6 million, 15% to 7.5 million, 20% to 9 million, 25% to 12 million and 30% above.
figures.applies: Annual basis. PwC's Chad pages were last reviewed on 12 August 2024; no 2026 source was found to confirm or change them (see blocker).

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year.
figures.applies: Return date not read. PwC's Chad pages were last reviewed on 12 August 2024; no 2026 source was found to confirm or change them (see blocker).

sources.said: The tax year in Chad is the calendar year.

figures.finding: The employer pays 16.5% and the employee 3.5% of gross pay, each on pay up to XAF 500,000 a month.
figures.applies: PwC's Chad pages were last reviewed on 12 August 2024; no 2026 source was found to confirm or change them (see blocker).

sources.said: Employer contributions are 16.5% of the gross salary limited to XAF 500,000 per month (XAF 82,500 upper limit). Employee contributions are 3.5% of the gross salary limited to XAF 500,000 per month (XAF 17,500 upper limit).

figures.finding: A non-resident is taxed on income from activities in Chad; income paid to a person resident outside the CEMAC area bears 25% withholding (20% for an individual resident in CEMAC).
figures.applies: PwC's Chad pages were last reviewed on 12 August 2024; no 2026 source was found to confirm or change them (see blocker).

sources.said: A non-resident individual in Chad is subject to PIT on the income stemming from activities in Chad.
WHT on income of non-residents is 25%. It applies to income of any legal or natural person who is not resident in the CEMAC area

figures.finding: VAT is 18% (9% on some local products).
figures.applies: Threshold not read. PwC's Chad pages were last reviewed on 12 August 2024; no 2026 source was found to confirm or change them (see blocker).

sources.said: The VAT rate applicable in Chad is: 18% on all taxable operations. 9% on local products
